tasks.label: Update and upgrade Homebrew, npm
tasks.command: brew update && brew upgrade --yes && npm update -g

tasks.label: Install local skills globally: development-best-practices
tasks.detail: Publish this repo's development-best-practices skill globally (copies to ~/.agents/skills/, symlinks to ~/.claude/skills/). Cross-project by nature: git branch and worktree hygiene, day-to-day dev workflow conventions.
tasks.command: npx --yes skills add ./.agents/skills/development-best-practices --agent claude-code --agent opencode --agent codex --global --yes

tasks.label: Install local skills globally: python-styleguide
tasks.detail: Publish this repo's python-styleguide skill globally (copies to ~/.agents/skills/, symlinks to ~/.claude/skills/). Cross-project by nature: shared Python style rules for all internal projects.
tasks.command: npx --yes skills add ./.agents/skills/python-styleguide --agent claude-code --agent opencode --agent codex --global --yes

tasks.label: Install local skills globally: all
tasks.detail: Publish every locally-authored skill worth having in all projects (runs each install task in sequence). Always --global by design: these skills already live in .agents/skills/, so a project-scope install would copy them onto themselves and the duplicate would silently drift. Keep this list minimal — OpenCode reads ~/.agents/skills/ directly, so every skill here costs context in every session of every project.

tasks.label: Link .claude/skills to .agents/skills
tasks.detail: Symlink the whole .claude/skills directory to .agents/skills, so Claude Code sees every project skill (it only scans .claude/skills/; OpenCode reads .agents/skills/ directly). Linking the directory rather than each skill means new skills need no re-run. Refuses if .claude/skills holds a real entry absent from .agents/skills, which would be lost.
tasks.command: cd "${workspaceFolder}" && if [ -L .claude/skills ]; then echo 'Already a symlink: .claude/skills -> '$(readlink .claude/skills); else if [ -d .claude/skills ]; then orphans=$(for e in .claude/skills/*; do [ -e "$e" ] || [ -L "$e" ] || continue; n=$(basename "$e"); if [ ! -L "$e" ] && [ ! -e ".agents/skills/$n" ]; then echo "$n"; fi; done); if [ -n "$orphans" ]; then echo "Refusing: .claude/skills holds entries absent from .agents/skills: $orphans" >&2; exit 1; fi; fi; rm -rf .claude/skills; mkdir -p .claude; ln -s ../.agents/skills .claude/skills; echo 'Linked .claude/skills -> ../.agents/skills'; fi

tasks.label: Link CLAUDE.md to AGENTS.md
tasks.detail: Replace CLAUDE.md with a symlink to AGENTS.md so both Claude Code and other agents read one instruction file. Refuses to clobber a CLAUDE.md that holds its own content — delete it manually first if that is intended.
tasks.command: cd "${workspaceFolder}" && if [ -L CLAUDE.md ]; then echo 'CLAUDE.md is already a symlink -> '$(readlink CLAUDE.md); elif [ -s CLAUDE.md ] && [ -n "$(grep -vE '^\s*(#.*)?$' CLAUDE.md | grep -viF 'AGENTS.md')" ]; then echo 'Refusing: CLAUDE.md has its own content. Review and delete it first.' >&2; exit 1; else rm -f CLAUDE.md && ln -s AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md && echo 'Linked CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md'; fi

tasks.label: Link Claude Code to project files
tasks.detail: Point Claude Code at this project's shared agent files: CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md and .claude/skills -> .agents/skills (runs both link tasks in sequence). Safe to re-run; both tasks are idempotent.

tasks.label: Install remote skills: logfire
tasks.detail: Install the upstream logfire skills from pydantic/skills for Claude Code and OpenCode. Skills are named explicitly because the repo also ships unrelated skills. Prompts for install scope (default: this project). Tracked in a skills lock file, so 'Update skills from remote sources' refreshes them.
tasks.command: npx --yes skills add pydantic/skills --skill logfire-instrumentation --skill logfire-query --skill logfire-ui --agent claude-code --agent opencode ${input:skillScope} --yes

tasks.label: Install remote skills: supabase
tasks.detail: Install the upstream supabase skills from supabase/agent-skills for Claude Code and OpenCode. Prompts for install scope (default: this project). Tracked in a skills lock file, so 'Update skills from remote sources' refreshes them.
tasks.command: npx --yes skills add supabase/agent-skills --skill supabase --skill supabase-postgres-best-practices --agent claude-code --agent opencode ${input:skillScope} --yes

tasks.label: Install remote skills: skill-creator
tasks.detail: Install Anthropic's skill-creator from anthropics/skills for Claude Code and OpenCode. Used instead of superpowers' writing-skills for authoring and evaluating skills. Prompts for install scope (default: this project).
tasks.command: npx --yes skills add anthropics/skills --skill skill-creator --agent claude-code --agent opencode ${input:skillScope} --yes

tasks.label: Install remote skills: superpowers subset
tasks.detail: Install the three superpowers skills worth keeping (brainstorming, systematic-debugging, writing-plans) from obra/superpowers, without the plugin's always-on SessionStart context injection. Prompts for install scope (default: this project).
tasks.command: npx --yes skills add obra/superpowers --skill brainstorming --skill systematic-debugging --skill writing-plans --agent claude-code --agent opencode ${input:skillScope} --yes

tasks.label: Install remote skills: all
tasks.detail: Install every remote-sourced skill (runs all install tasks in sequence). Each prompts for scope. On-demand: these are not installed by default to keep agent context small.

tasks.label: Update skills from remote sources
tasks.detail: Re-fetch all skills tracked in ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json from their remote sources and re-copy if changed
tasks.command: npx skills update --yes

tasks.label: Sync OpenCode config globally
tasks.detail: Copy this project's OpenCode, TUI, and DCP configs plus the .mcp.json loader and schema to ~/.config/opencode. Shows a diff unless you type 'yes'.
tasks.command: bash "${workspaceFolder}/scripts/sync_files.sh" --confirm=${input:syncConfirm} "${workspaceFolder}/.opencode/opencode.jsonc" "$HOME/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc" "${workspaceFolder}/.opencode/tui.json" "$HOME/.config/opencode/tui.json" "${workspaceFolder}/.opencode/dcp.jsonc" "$HOME/.config/opencode/dcp.jsonc" "${workspaceFolder}/.opencode/plugins/load-mcp-json.js" "$HOME/.config/opencode/plugins/load-mcp-json.js" "${workspaceFolder}/.opencode/schemas/claude-mcp.schema.json" "$HOME/.config/opencode/schemas/claude-mcp.schema.json"

tasks.label: Sync Claude settings globally
tasks.detail: Copy this project's Claude Code settings to ~/.claude/settings.json. Shows a diff unless you type 'yes'. Note this replaces the file wholesale — any global-only keys (e.g. a permissions.allow list) are dropped, so read the diff before confirming.
tasks.command: bash "${workspaceFolder}/scripts/sync_files.sh" --confirm=${input:syncConfirm} "${workspaceFolder}/.claude/settings.json" "$HOME/.claude/settings.json"

tasks.label: Sync VSCode settings and tasks to Devin User
tasks.detail: Overwrite Devin User settings.json and tasks.json with workspace .vscode config. Shows a diff unless you type 'yes'.
tasks.command: bash "${workspaceFolder}/scripts/sync_files.sh" --confirm=${input:syncConfirm} "${workspaceFolder}/.vscode/settings.json" "$HOME/Library/Application Support/Devin/User/settings.json" "${workspaceFolder}/.vscode/tasks.json" "$HOME/Library/Application Support/Devin/User/tasks.json"

tasks.label: List running OpenCode processes
tasks.detail: Print the PID and working directory of each running OpenCode process
tasks.command: bash "${workspaceFolder}/scripts/list-opencode-processes.sh"

tasks.label: Caffeinate process
tasks.detail: Prevent idle system sleep until the process with the provided PID exits
tasks.command: caffeinate -i -w ${input:pid}

tasks.label: OKF AI-engineering: regenerate index
tasks.detail: Regenerate index.md for the ai-engineering OKF bundle from concept frontmatter
tasks.command: uv run --project . python .agents/skills/okf/scripts/okf_index.py .agents/skills/okf-ai-engineering/ai-engineering

tasks.label: OKF AI-engineering: install skill
tasks.detail: Install only the okf-ai-engineering skill globally via npx skills (copies to ~/.agents/skills/, symlinks to ~/.claude/skills/)
tasks.command: npx --yes skills add ./.agents/skills/okf-ai-engineering --agent claude-code --agent opencode --agent codex --global --yes

tasks.label: OKF AI-engineering: regenerate index & install skill
OKF AI-engineering: build site
tasks.detail: Regenerate okf-site.html for the ai-engineering OKF bundle
tasks.command: uv run --project . python .agents/skills/okf/scripts/okf_site.py .agents/skills/okf-ai-engineering/ai-engineering

tasks.label: OKF AI-engineering: open site
tasks.detail: Open the generated ai-engineering OKF site in the browser
tasks.command: open .agents/skills/okf-ai-engineering/ai-engineering/okf-site.html

tasks.label: OKF AI-engineering: build & open site
tasks.detail: Build and then open the ai-engineering OKF site

tasks.label: OKF AI-engineering: regenerate index, install skill, build and open site
tasks.detail: Regenerate the index, install the skill, build and open the site (runs all three in sequence)
dependsOn: OKF AI-engineering: regenerate index & install skill

tasks.label: Create worktree and open in IDE
tasks.command: bash scripts/create_worktree.sh ${input:worktreeBranch} ${input:worktreeDir}

tasks.label: Get venv packages size
tasks.command: uv run python -c "from dima.get_venv_packages_size import main; main()"

tasks.label: Install pre-commit
tasks.command: pre-commit install --hook-type pre-commit --hook-type commit-msg --hook-type pre-push

tasks.label: Run pre-commit
tasks.command: uv run pre-commit run --all-files || uv run pre-commit run --all-files

tasks.label: Login to aws
tasks.command: aws sso login --profile ${AWS_PROFILE}

tasks.label: Login to aws docker registry
tasks.command: aws --profile ${AWS_PROFILE} ecr get-login-password --region ${AWS_DEFAULT_REGION} | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin ${DOCKER_REPO}

tasks.label: Get opencode stats
tasks.command: opencode stats --project '' --models --days ${input:days}

inputs.description: Branch name for the new worktree
Optional worktree directory (absolute, or relative to <repo>/.worktrees/; defaults to normalized branch name)
Type 'yes' to overwrite the destination files; anything else only prints the diff
PID of the process to caffeinate
Number of days to look back
